subject: environmental-science
title: Biodiversity & Wildlife: Helping Wildlife
welcome_lead: Small actions help wildlife big time — from planting flowers to nature reserves.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: conservation, reserves, rewilding.
final_note: Anyone with a window box can help.

concepts.def: Protected area set aside for wildlife.
Animal that moves pollen, like a bee.
Backyard space — can be wildlife friendly.

walkthroughs.body_html: Nature reserves protect important habitats. The UK has thousands, from peat bogs to seabird cliffs.
Rewilding brings back lost species and lets ecosystems rebuild. Beavers, for example, have returned to many UK rivers.
Plant flowers for bees, leave a bit of garden messy, put out a bird feeder. Join a citizen science project to record what you see.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.
Water vapour released from plant leaves to the atmosphere.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Water flowing through soil into rivers.
